draft.title: Evidence, opinion and anecdote
card: Evidence
information gathered by a planned, tested method, such as an experiment or a survey. Other researchers can check the method and repeat it.
Opinion
what a person believes or feels about a topic. It may be well meant, but it does not come from a tested method.
Anecdote
a personal story about one case or a few cases. It is not a planned test, so it may not apply to other people.
Opinions and anecdotes can suggest ideas to test. They cannot settle a question, because nobody can check them in a repeatable way.
draft.remember: Evidence can be tested and repeated. Opinions and anecdotes can suggest ideas, but cannot settle a question.

a.q: Which of these is scientific evidence about sleep and memory?
opts: A planned experiment on rested and tired students' scores
A teacher's belief that tired students always remember less
A student's story about failing a test after a late night
A famous coach saying sleep is the best way to learn
a.why: A planned experiment uses a tested method that others can check and repeat. The teacher's belief is an opinion, and the student's story is an anecdote, so neither is a tested method.
a.clue: Look for the planned method that others could repeat.

b.q: Priya's uncle says his cousin quit social media and felt much happier, so everyone should quit. Why can this not settle whether quitting social media improves mood?
opts: It is an anecdote about one person, and it was not tested
It is an opinion, so it must be false
It is evidence, but it is too old to use
It is an anecdote, so it cannot suggest any ideas to test
b.why: The story is about one case and was not a planned, repeatable test, so it may not apply to others. It is wrong to say it must be false or cannot suggest an idea: anecdotes can suggest ideas to test, but they cannot settle the question.
b.clue: One case, with no planned method, cannot decide it for everyone.
